items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: They were very generous. Dave Love.

ctx.x: I assume this is not a record Telarc would be interested in.

Telarc’s over, anyway, because Dave’s not there anymore. No. They paid $50,000 for each of those records. I’m telling you. By the time we were in and out. They were very generous. Dave Love. They didn’t – they sold some of the first ones, because of Michael. I got to say about Michael also, it was very generous, because the money was split three ways. We paid sidemen what we paid him. Even that was, at the beginning was – because the manager was like – Michael’s manager took care of the business, who gets who,…

money,” blah blah blah blah. Michael was a sweetheart. But I would get this from the manager. “He’s taking quite a cut, you know,” which means, he’s taking a cut. So actually he was making less than me, because he had to give away 10 or 15 percent, which I didn’t have, because I don’t have a manager. So I ended up making more than the other two guys, probably, because Joe had to give it to his manager, I guess. I don’t know how they work. It’s not my business.
